articles.title: US lawmakers seek federal probe into disruption of Seattle Diwali event over racist signs
articles.summary: US lawmakers Grace Meng, Pramila Jayapal and Raja Krishnamoorthi have sought a federal investigation into the disruption of a Diwali celebration in
articles.body: US lawmakers Grace Meng, Pramila Jayapal and Raja Krishnamoorthi have sought a federal investigation into the disruption of a Diwali celebration in Seattle, Washington, allegedly by two men who entered the venue carrying signs with racial slurs and hateful messages. One of the signs reportedly demanded the deportation of Indian Americans.In a letter, the lawmakers expressed concern over the incident involving Jake Lang and Thomas Allen, accusing the two of disrupting the cultural celebration with racist messages targeting the Indian American community.The letter was led by Grace Meng, chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (CAPAC), along with Pramila Jayapal and Raja Krishnamoorthi.“It is vital that those of us entrusted with public offices confront hate wherever it appears. No family should have to wonder whether it is safe to light a lamp, perform a dance, or bring their children to a festival in their own city,” wrote the lawmakers. “The events in Seattle follow a troubling series of threats against South Asian communities across the country.”The lawmakers also raised concerns over the backgrounds of Lang and Allen, alleging that both had records of reckless and criminal conduct. They specifically cited Lang's assault on police officers during the January 6 Capitol riot, for which he was later pardoned by US President Donald Trump.According to the letter, Lang and Allen were promoting the so-called "replacement" theory, which the lawmakers described as a false narrative claiming that non-white and non-Christian people were being brought into the US to replace white Christian Americans.The lawmakers also linked the incident to what they described as rising anti-South Asian hate across the US, alleging that the Trump administration had contributed to such hostility.“When the Department of Homeland Security publishes a graphic mocking a Sikh man with the message, ‘Get off our roads, you don’t know how to drive Mr. Singh,’ it should come as no surprise that Mr. Lang and Mr. Allen were emboldened to disrupt a cultural celebration and boast a racist sign demanding that Indian Americans be deported,” the lawmakers wrote.They said the actions of Lang and Allen could potentially constitute hate crimes under multiple federal statutes.The letter cited Section 245 of Title 18 of the US Code, which prohibits the use of force or threats to intimidate individuals on the basis of race, colour, religion or national origin, including for participating in or patronising public accommodations.It also referred to Section 241 of Title 18, which prohibits intimidating or oppressing individuals exercising rights guaranteed under the Constitution, and Section 247, which criminalises obstructing a person's religious practices through force or threats.Apart from seeking a federal probe into the Seattle incident, the lawmakers urged the department of justice (DOJ) to prioritise hate crime investigations and restore funding and resources to its Community Relations Service.The agency, established under the Civil Rights Act, works with communities to resolve conflicts. However, the lawmakers alleged that the Trump administration had significantly weakened the agency.The full text of the letter was made public by the lawmakers.The letter was also signed by Representatives Yassamin Ansari, Ami Bera, Judy Chu, Suzan K. DelBene, Ro Khanna, Emily Randall, Lateefah Simon, Adam Smith, Suhas Subramanyam and Shri Thanedar.This comes after a Diwali celebration in Seattle was disrupted when far-right American activist Jake Lang and a group of protesters attempted to interrupt the festivities, carrying placards that read "Deport All Dot Heads".You use AI every day. articles.title: Ghaziabad man pays Rs 1,760 online for two ladies' suits for wife in Nov 2023; Delhi boutique fails to deliver despite repeated requests; 3 years later consumer commission orders refund with 6% interest and Rs 2,000 compensation
articles.summary: GHAZIABAD: A Delhi-based boutique has been directed to refund Rs 1,760 to a customer for two ladies’ suits it failed to deliver despite receiving online
articles.body: GHAZIABAD: A Delhi-based boutique has been directed to refund Rs 1,760 to a customer for two ladies’ suits it failed to deliver despite receiving online payment in Nov 2023. The district consumer disputes redressal commission has also ordered the firm to pay 6% annual interest on the amount from the date of payment until the refund is made, along with Rs 2,000 in compensation for mental harassment.The order, passed on Oct 29 by commission president Anil Kumar Pundir and members Shailja Sachan and RP Singh, directs the boutique to comply within 30 days. If it fails to do so, the interest rate on the outstanding amount will increase to 9% per annum until payment, the commission said.The case arose from a complaint filed on May 13, 2024, by Zahid Ali, a resident of Ghaziabad, against Delhi-based M/s CK Enterprises through its proprietor, Pooja Dahiya. Ali said he had ordered two ladies’ suits for his wife and paid Rs 1,760 online on Nov 16, 2023. Although the payment was accepted and acknowledged by the proprietor, the suits were not delivered despite repeated requests, and his calls went unanswered.Ali alleged that the firm’s conduct amounted to an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act. The commission issued notices to the proprietor and the firm, but neither responded. With no written reply or representation through a lawyer, the commission proceeded ex parte on July 9, 2024.After examining Ali’s affidavit and supporting documents and hearing his counsel, the commission noted that the respondents had neither appeared despite being served notice nor contested the allegations.“Therefore, the available evidence proves that the plaintiff made the payment and the defendants did not supply the goods. The defendants’ actions constitute deficiency in service and unfair trade practices,” the commission observed, ruling that Ali was entitled to a refund with interest and compensation for the mental harassment caused.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Noida | Silver Rate in Noida | Bank Holidays in Noida | Public Holidays in Noida | Noida AQI | Weather in Noida | Petrol Price in Noida | Diesel Price in Noida | CNG Price in Noida | LPG Price in NoidaStay updated with the latest Noida news. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar filed an affidavit in Supreme Court on Tuesday saying permission to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar filed an affidavit in Supreme Court on Tuesday saying permission to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar on Oct 10 was denied given Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) non-compliance with past undertakings for peaceful protest and intelligence inputs pointing towards a possible “dangerous situation” causing a serious public order problem.“A major public order situation was averted (on Oct 10) by timely, proportionate and lawful measures taken by Delhi Police,” the commissioner said, adding, “Keeping this scenario in mind, certain preventive steps were required to be taken. One such step was to prevent anyone to become part of an unlawful assembly and to participate in commission of cognisable offences as a consequence of assembling at Jantar Mantar.” In his affidavit, Kumar said all protesters, including politicians, who were removed from Jantar Mantar on Oct 10 were neither detained nor arrested but kept in makeshift centres or in the SHO’s room in police stations and were provided with refreshments.Also Read| SC to hear INDIA bloc's poser plea on CEC on Dec 9Kumar said SC must take a holistic view of the matter, its sensitivity and the preventive measures taken by police. “No police administration can permit breach of public order in the national capital, particularly when a call is given by an organisation with a recent history of mob violence, destruction of public and private property, and incidents resulting in injuries to several individuals and the subsequent protests (by Congress) on Oct 6, 7, 8,” he said. “Certain regulatory measures were introduced for regulating 57 Metro stations on Oct 9 but the same was reviewed pursuant to the SC order and only 45 of 303 Metro stations were regulated,” he added.Dealing with law and order was a highly sensitive aspect of policing, requiring a delicate balance between the right to protest of some on the one hand, and the rights of other citizens to lead their normal and peaceful life, he said. The potential danger to life and property of citizens and public property also needed to be kept in mind, he added.Kumar said CJP was given permission to hold a peaceful protest for a day on June 20 and it had given an undertaking that the number of protesters would be around 1,000. articles.title: A Seattle developer pledged a $300 million art collection to a university, but 50 artworks are now going to auction to repay a loan backed by the artwork; the remaining 350 pieces are still promised to the school
articles.summary: A collection of paintings by some of the world's most celebrated artists was expected to become one of the biggest cultural gifts to an American
articles.body: A collection of paintings by some of the world's most celebrated artists was expected to become one of the biggest cultural gifts to an American university. However, a financial arrangement involving the artworks has changed that plan, with dozens of pieces now heading to auction instead of a university museum. The sale involves a collection originally valued at $300 million and pledged by Seattle real estate developer and philanthropist Richard 'Dick' Hedreen to Seattle University.In a September 14, 2026, update to its community, Seattle University confirmed that Hedreen had decided to sell approximately 50 artworks while reaffirming his commitment to donate the remaining 350 pieces in honour of his late wife, Betty Hedreen. A November 13 report by The Seattle Times explained that the auction is intended to repay an outstanding loan secured against the collection. The sale is therefore not primarily a fundraising exercise for the university but an effort to clear the debt before the promised donation can become an outright gift.A $300 million collection was pledged to Seattle UniversityThe collection was assembled over several decades by Hedreen and his late wife, Betty, who was a Seattle University alumna. Their interest in art began with purchasing a few pieces for their home before gradually developing into a major private collection spanning several centuries of artistic history. In March 2024, Seattle University announced that Hedreen was donating the collection, valued at more than $300 million, along with what was described as $25 million in seed funding for a new art museum. The university presented it as the largest gift of art ever made to a US university.The collection includes paintings, sculptures, photography, pottery and prints by internationally recognised artists, including Titian, Willem de Kooning, Roy Lichtenstein, Thomas Gainsborough, Robert Rauschenberg and David Hockney. The proposed museum was intended to display these works while supporting art education, research and public exhibitions.However, the arrangement was a pledge to donate the collection in the future rather than an immediate transfer of ownership. This distinction became important when the financial circumstances surrounding the artworks changed.Why 50 artworks are being sold at auctionThe auction involves approximately 50 artworks, with proceeds intended to repay a loan secured against part of the collection. The Seattle Times reported that records show an associated company first offered paintings as security to Goldman Sachs in 2012. In 2025, a Bank of America loan replaced the earlier arrangement, with approximately 44 major artworks serving as collateral. The outstanding loan was not publicly disclosed, but the artworks' estimated values suggested that it could exceed $100 million. At least 18 of the approximately 50 pieces being offered through Sotheby's are reportedly connected to the loan.The Seattle Times reported that among the works being offered are Roy Lichtenstein's Reflections on 'Painter and Model', estimated at $20 million to $30 million, and de Kooning's Water...Soft Banks and a Window (Untitled VIII), carrying a similar estimate. Sam Francis' Towards Disappearance has an estimated value of $15 million to $20 million. The overall Sotheby's sale is expected to generate between $109 million and $158 million. The financial pressures in the hotel and real estate sectors contributed to the decision. R.C. Hedreen Co. President David Thyer said income from the company's hotels was insufficient to repay the loan within a reasonably foreseeable period.Hedreen's son, Guy, told The Seattle Times that the sale was intended to remove the debt preventing his father from completing the university donation. He also said the family and university had jointly selected the works being sold to preserve the quality and diversity of the remaining collection.What happens to the remaining 350 artworks and the museum?Seattle University has reiterated that the planned donation remains in place. In its September statement, university president Maura B. Mast, provost Shane P. Martin and senior vice-president for university advancement Edgar Gonzalez said Hedreen had reaffirmed his commitment to gift approximately 350 remaining works in memory of his wife. The university's proposed Seattle University Museum of Art is also moving forward, although its construction timeline has changed. The project, designed by Seattle architect Tom Kundig, was originally expected to begin construction in 2026 but has been pushed to 2027 as permitting continues.The approximately $65 million museum project is expected to include permanent galleries, rotating exhibitions, classrooms, an event space and a cafe. The university has raised $55 million towards the development, including $17 million from the private sale of a de Kooning painting that had been valued at $25 million when it was announced as seed funding in 2024. The remaining collection is expected to form the museum's permanent holdings, although its final composition and donation timeline have not been confirmed.The situation highlights the difference between promising an artwork as a future gift and legally transferring ownership. Hedreen's son, Guy, told The Seattle Times that the pledge agreement allowed his father to buy and sell artworks until the collection was officially transferred to Seattle University. The agreement has not been made public, but the family maintains that the remaining collection will still be donated to the university.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: From Rajasthan painting to Kashmiri carpet: What PM Modi gifted to Asean, Quad leaders during Manila visit
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi presented a range of traditional Indian artworks and handicrafts to world leaders during his visit to Manila, the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi presented a range of traditional Indian artworks and handicrafts to world leaders during his visit to Manila, the Philippines, offering gifts that showcased the country's diverse regional craftsmanship, textile traditions and cultural heritage.The gifts included a Golden Pichwaai painting from Rajasthan for US President Donald Trump, a traditional Kashmiri silk carpet for Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr and a Chola bronze sculpture for Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto.PM Modi also presented a Dokra artwork boat to Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet, Bidriware silver inlay vases to Myanmar and Brunei, a royal blue Banarasi silk stole to Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, and a Jaipur blue pottery artefact to Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.The presents drew on traditional art forms and crafts from different parts of India, including Rajasthan, Kashmir, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh and the Deccan region.What Modi gifted to Trump, Marcos and other leadersUS President Donald Trump: Golden Pichwaai paintingPM Modi gifted Trump a Golden Pichwaai painting from Nathdwara in Rajasthan. The traditional cloth-painting art is known for its intricate detailing, luminous colours and elaborate compositions.Created on finely prepared cloth using mineral pigments and gold detailing, Pichwaai paintings feature motifs such as lotuses, cows and trees, along with ornamental borders. Their golden finish gives the artwork a distinctive regal appearance.Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr: Kashmiri silk carpetThe Philippine President received a traditional Kashmiri silk carpet, a hand-knotted craft admired for its sheen, soft texture, intricate designs and durability.Made from fine silk, the carpets involve thousands of knots tied by skilled artisans. Some take months or even years to complete. Their designs often draw inspiration from Kashmir's natural beauty, featuring floral patterns, chinar leaves and geometric motifs.Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto: Chola bronze sculpturePM Modi presented a traditional Chola bronze sculpture to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto. The art form flourished between the ninth and thirteenth centuries under the Chola dynasty in South India.The sculptures are made using the traditional lost-wax casting technique, known as Madhuchista Vidhana. Each piece is individually handcrafted, making it unique.Known for their anatomical precision, graceful forms and expressive details, Chola bronzes also offer insights into the clothing, jewellery, hairstyles and artistic traditions of the period. They represent Tamil Nadu's metallurgical skills and artistic heritage.Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim: Silver worked urliPM Modi gifted Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim a traditional silver worked urli, a decorative Indian vessel adorned with intricate silver embellishments that showcase the skill of the country's metalworkers.Traditionally filled with water and decorated with floating flowers, the urli symbolises purity, prosperity, hospitality and harmony.Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet: Dokra artwork boatCambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet received a traditional Dokra artwork boat. The metal craft is made using the lost-wax casting technique, a tradition dating back more than 4,000 years.The handcrafted piece depicts a boat carrying figures and birds, reflecting community life and harmony with nature. Each artwork is individually modelled in wax before being cast in metal.The boat symbolises unity, cooperation, resilience and collective progress. The craft also preserves traditional skills and supports artisan livelihoods.Myanmar and Brunei: Bidriware silver inlay vasesPM Modi gifted Bidriware silver inlay vases from Bidar, Karnataka, to Myanmar and Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah of Brunei.Bidriware is a traditional metal craft made from a zinc-and-copper alloy and decorated with intricate pure silver inlay. Artisans engrave patterns, insert silver wire and treat the surface to create its characteristic deep black finish, which contrasts with the silver designs.The floral and geometric motifs draw inspiration from the architectural heritage of Bidar Fort. The craft has a Geographical Indication (GI) tag and represents the artistic traditions of the Deccan region.Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi: Banarasi Katan silk stoleJapanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi received a royal blue Banarasi Katan silk stole presented in a Sadheli box.Woven from fine Katan silk, the stole showcases the centuries-old textile traditions of Banaras. Its intricate motifs reflect the craftsmanship and precision of generations of weavers.The royal blue colour symbolises dignity, wisdom and harmony, while the presentation in a Sadheli box represents India's warmth and cultural esteem.Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese: Jaipur blue pottery artefactPM Modi gifted Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese a traditional Jaipur blue pottery artefact from Rajasthan.The craft is known for its glossy white surface and luminous cobalt-blue designs. Its pieces feature hand-painted floral patterns, birds, geometric motifs and decorative borders.Lao Prime Minister Sonexay Siphandone: Rose quartz elephant with gold workPM Modi gifted Lao Prime Minister Sonexay Siphandone a rose quartz elephant with gold work, a decorative craft associated with Rajasthan's stone-carving centres, particularly Jaipur.The artwork is carved from natural rose quartz and polished to bring out its soft, translucent sheen. It is then decorated with intricate hand-painted gold detailing, floral motifs and traditional ornamental designs.Combining gemstone carving with miniature painting, the elephant symbolises strength, wisdom, dignity and royal grandeur in Indian tradition. Its gilded detailing reflects India's heritage of luxury handicrafts and royal decorative arts.Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul: Rogan art paintingThai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul received a traditional Rogan art painting from Kutch, Gujarat. Practised by a handful of artisan families in Nirona village, Rogan art is a rare, centuries-old textile painting tradition.The technique uses a thick, elastic paint prepared by boiling castor oil and mixing it with natural pigments. Artisans create intricate designs freehand on fabric using a slender metal stylus. The cloth is then folded to transfer a symmetrical mirror image onto the other half.Traditionally used in bridal trousseaus and festive attire, Rogan art is known for its intricate patterns, geometric precision and craftsmanship. It represents Kutch's cultural heritage and the ingenuity of its artisans.Timor-Leste Prime Minister Kay Rala Xanana Gusmão: Handcrafted agate bowlPM Modi gifted Timor-Leste Prime Minister Kay Rala Xanana Gusmão a handcrafted agate bowl from Khambhat, Gujarat. Made from agate, a semi-precious gemstone, each bowl has distinctive natural bands, colours and textures, making every piece unique.Khambhat has been a centre of agate processing and stone carving for centuries. Skilled artisans carefully cut, shape and polish the stone to create decorative and functional objects.Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung: Traditional Indian leather wall hangingVietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung received a traditional Indian leather wall hanging, a handcrafted decorative artwork rooted in the country's folk-art heritage.Artisans soften and stretch treated leather before creating intricate designs through perforation, embossing and painting. The artworks feature floral, geometric and wildlife motifs, often made using natural vegetable dyes.Rooted in rural traditions and passed down through generations, the craft reflects regional artistic styles and storytelling. It also helps preserve traditional skills and support artisan livelihoods.PM Modi's two-day visit to ManilaThe gifts were presented during PM Modi's November 16-17 visit to the Philippines, where he attended the 23rd Asean-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit. He also participated in a Quad leaders' meeting with Trump, Takaichi and Albanese.During the visit, India and Asean adopted a joint statement on cooperation in disaster management. The two sides also agreed to strengthen early warning systems, share satellite data, conduct joint simulation exercises and promote the use of artificial intelligence in disaster risk assessment and response coordination.PM Modi announced several initiatives to deepen India's engagement with the region, including a maritime cooperation plan, a joint cyber forensics training programme, technical exchanges on nuclear energy, a space hackathon and cooperation on critical minerals.Other announcements included youth and start-up initiatives, enhanced scholarships for Asean students at Nalanda University and free e-visas for tourists from Asean countries.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A Haryana advocate who paid Rs 18,400 to courier winter clothes and food items to Canada received them after 28 days; consumer commission ordered company to pay Rs 58,400 with 9% interest for delayed delivery
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A consumer commission in Haryana has held a courier company guilty of deficiency in service for delivering a shipment of clothes and edible
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A consumer commission in Haryana has held a courier company guilty of deficiency in service for delivering a shipment of clothes and edible items to Canada 28 days after accepting it, despite assuring delivery within 10-12 days.The commission directed Brand House to pay Rs 48,400 towards the value of the edible items and courier charges. It also ordered the firm to pay Rs 10,000 as compensation and litigation costs.In its November 5, 2026, order, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Rohtak, noted that the delay had defeated the purpose of sending the seasonal clothes and perishable food items to Canada.Courier firm delays delivery of food items and clothes to CanadaAccording to the commission order, Surender Dhokal, a 47-year-old advocate from Rohtak, had booked the services of Brand House on January 29, 2025, to send clothes and edible items to Canada.The shipment was booked on January 30, 2025, under tracking ID 1Z0V1Y572017007517. The complainant handed over the items to the firm's representative in Rohtak and was assured that they would be delivered within 10-15 days. He paid Rs 18,400 for a shipment weighing 21 kg through UPI.However, the complainant said the items were not delivered within the promised period. He claimed that the clothes were meant for the winter season and would become useless after the season ended. The edible and perishable items also became stale or unusable because of the delay. He valued the items at Rs 50,000.The complainant said he contacted the firm several times but did not receive a satisfactory response. He also sent a legal notice on February 27, 2025, but received no relief.He approached the commission seeking Rs 3 lakh for non-delivery within the promised period, Rs 50,000 as compensation for harassment and Rs 22,000 towards litigation expenses.Brand House did not appear before the commission despite receiving notice. It was proceeded against ex parte through an order dated May 22, 2025, and did not file its defence.Why commission held courier firm liableThe bench comprising president Nagender Singh Kadian and members Dr Tripti Pannu and Dr Vijender Singh noted that the complainant had submitted payment details, shipment documents, delivery receipt and WhatsApp conversations with the firm.The commission observed that the WhatsApp chats showed that the firm had assured delivery of the perishable items within 10-12 days. However, the delivery receipt showed that the shipment was delivered only on February 28, 2025, after 28 days.It said the delay could have made the perishable items stale, inedible or unusable. The clothes, too, could not serve their intended purpose because they were not delivered during the relevant season.The bench also noted that the firm had failed to appear despite service of notice, leaving the complainant's evidence unrebutted.“Perusal of the documents reveals that the items were delivered on 28.02.2025, i.e. after 28 days, as against the assured delivery period of 10-12 days. Due to such delay, the perishable items might have become stale, inedible or otherwise unusable. Further, the clothes, having not been delivered within the stipulated time, could not serve the intended purpose of the consignee at the relevant time,” the commission said.The commission further recorded that the complainant had submitted during arguments that the shipment included 10 kg of desi ghee laddus, valued at around Rs 30,000, considering the cost of desi ghee and dry fruits. He had also paid Rs 18,400 as courier charges.Considering the delay and the resulting loss, the bench said it would be just and proper to award Rs 30,000 towards the value of the edible items and Rs 18,400 towards courier charges.Final orderThe commission allowed the complaint and directed Brand House to:Pay Rs 48,400 towards the value of the edible items and courier charges, along with 9 percent annual interest from March 27, 2025, until realisation.Pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for mental agony and harassment.Pay Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses.The firm has been directed to comply with the order within 30 days of receiving a copy of it.

articles.title: Democrats flip 9 US senate seats, marking biggest midterm gain in nearly 70 years
articles.summary: Former US representative Mary Peltola has defeated Republican incumbent senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska's closely contested senate race, handing democrats
articles.body: Former US representative Mary Peltola has defeated Republican incumbent senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska's closely contested senate race, handing democrats their ninth victory in a republican-held seat. The result marks the party's biggest midterm senate gains in nearly seven decades, according to news agency AP.The last time democrats picked up nine or more senate seats during a midterm election was in 1958, when republican president Dwight Eisenhower was serving his second term. Democrats won 13 seats previously held by republicans that year and secured both of Alaska's newly established Senate seats, recording a total gain of 15 seats.Peltola's victory gives democrats a 56-44 majority in the Senate when the new Congress convenes in January. It will be the party's strongest senate advantage in 16 years. Democrats previously held 58 seats during the final days of the 111th Congress, which ended on January 3, 2011.Even without the Alaska result, democrats would have achieved their largest senate majority since January 2015. Republicans took control of the chamber that year after gaining nine democratic-held seats in the 2014 midterm elections, held during president Barack Obama's second term.Earlier, democrat Scott Colom's victory in Mississippi's Senate race on Wednesday had given his party its eighth pickup from republican-held seats. The result marked democrats' biggest midterm senate gains since the second midterm election of president Ronald Reagan, 40 years ago.Democrats have also regained control of the house of representatives, securing 42 additional seats as of Tuesday. Their gains reflect a longstanding electoral pattern in which the president's party typically suffers losses during midterm elections.Historically, the senate has been less vulnerable to the midterm effect than the house. In seven of the 16 midterm elections before 2026, the president's party either maintained its Senate strength or added seats. However, all but one of those elections took place during a president's first term, with second-term midterms generally proving more damaging.The trend has been considerably stronger in the house, where the president's party has managed to gain seats in just two midterm elections since the end of world war II.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast thunderstorms, lightning, gusty winds and rainfall across several states over the next few days. Cyclonic Storm Akvan is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm, bringing heavy to extremely heavy rainfall to parts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and neighbouring states. Meanwhile, dense fog is likely to affect Delhi-NCR and adjoining northern states.Delhi-NCR weather tomorrowThe IMD has forecast dense fog at isolated places over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh and Punjab until November 20. East and West Uttar Pradesh are also likely to experience dense fog during this period.The weather department has not provided a specific temperature forecast for Delhi in its latest bulletin.Cyclone Akvan: Andhra Pradesh weather tomorrowCyclonic Storm Akvan, currently over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal, is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm by November 19.According to the IMD, the system is expected to move northwestwards and cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around noon on November 20.At the time of landfall, the storm is likely to bring maximum sustained winds of 120-130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph.The IMD has issued an Orange Message cyclone alert for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts.In coastal Andhra Pradesh, light to moderate rainfall is likely at several places, with heavy rainfall at isolated locations on November 18. Extremely heavy rainfall, exceeding 21 cm, is likely at isolated places over north coastal Andhra Pradesh on November 19 and 20.Odisha weather tomorrowThe IMD has forecast light to moderate rainfall at some places in Odisha, with heavy rainfall at isolated locations on November 18.Rainfall is likely to intensify between November 19 and 21, with light to moderate showers at most places and heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated locations.Meanwhile, the Rayagada district administration has identified around 55 landslide-prone villages for possible evacuation and stepped up preparedness ahead of Cyclone Akvan.Located along the Andhra Pradesh border, Rayagada has been issued yellow and orange warnings for November 19 and 20, with heavy rainfall expected.Northeast India weather tomorrowAssam and Meghalaya are likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall between November 19 and 22. Isolated thunderstorms and lightning are also expected over the two states on November 18 and 19.Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura may experience isolated to scattered rainfall on November 22. Thunderstorms and lightning are likely over these states on November 19 and 20.Tamil Nadu weather tomorrowThe IMD has forecast light to moderate rainfall at many places over north Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on November 17 and 20, with heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places on November 19.The rainfall could lead to waterlogging in parts of Tamil Nadu.Telangana weather tomorrowCyclone Akvan is also likely to influence weather conditions in Telangana after crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast.Four eastern districts of Telangana have been placed under an orange alert for November 20, with the possibility of heavy rainfall as the cyclonic system moves inland.IMD's latest forecast for the next few daysThe IMD said Cyclone Akvan was located approximately 610 km east of Chennai, 630 km northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 660 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 670 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 790 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha.The system is likely to continue moving northwestwards before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast around noon on November 20 as a very severe cyclonic storm.The IMD has advised authorities and residents in the coastal regions covered by the warnings to remain alert and follow official advisories.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: 12 people board Kanpur-Delhi Vande Bharat to help relatives settle in, automatic doors shut before they can get off, group carried 139km to Etawah and get fined Rs 36,000
articles.summary: KANPUR: Twelve people who boarded the Kanpur-Delhi Vande Bharat Express to help their relatives settle into their seats were left stranded on the train
articles.body: KANPUR: Twelve people who boarded the Kanpur-Delhi Vande Bharat Express to help their relatives settle into their seats were left stranded on the train after its automatic doors shut before they could get off.The group was carried 139 km to Etawah, where the Railway Protection Force (RPF) fined them Rs 3,000 each, collecting a total of Rs 36,000 for travelling without valid tickets.The 12 had entered train no. 22415, running from Banaras to New Delhi, at Kanpur Central to help family members board. However, before they could get off, the train's automatic doors closed and it pulled out of the station.Realising they were on the wrong side of the closed doors, they approached train staff and requested that the doors be opened. However, this was not possible as the train was moving. Vande Bharat's automatic doors can be opened only when the train halts at designated stations and shut after a fixed interval.Women and children were among the 12 people stranded on board. The unexpected journey triggered panic, with some passengers objecting and creating a disturbance. However, the train could not be stopped midway to let them off.The group finally got off at Etawah, around 139 km from Kanpur. RPF personnel subsequently imposed a fine of Rs 3,000 on each of them for travelling without valid tickets.Shivam Sharma, chief public relations officer of North Central Railway, said unauthorised entry into Vande Bharat coaches was prohibited.He said the 12 had boarded the train without platform tickets while seeing off their relatives. articles.title: Cornered in a mosque, said 'no' to surrender: How forces killed LeT commander Lateef Bhat
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Top Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commander Lateef Bhat was killed in an encounter with security forces on Wednesday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Top Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commander Lateef Bhat was killed in an encounter with security forces on Wednesday. Bhat was involved in the November 11 attack on Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district.Bhat was considered the most wanted terrorist in Kashmir and the only surviving local terrorist in the Valley.The encounter began early Wednesday morning following specific intelligence inputs. Security forces launched a focused cordon-and-search operation after re-establishing contact with Bhat, who had escaped from the site of an earlier encounter in the Laru bypass area on Monday.Dar was killed in that gunfight on Monday, but Bhat managed to escape. Security forces subsequently continued extensive searches across the surrounding area to track him down.SSP Kulgam Anayat Ali said the operation was based on credible intelligence from Jammu and Kashmir Police and involved detailed planning and coordination among security forces. Bhat was cornered during the operation and repeatedly urged to surrender."We made extensive efforts to appeal to him to surrender and spoke with him. I personally had a video call with him, and I spoke with him for a fairly long time through a phone provided inside. We tried hard to persuade him to surrender, telling him that he is still young and has his whole life ahead of him. He did not agree and entered a mosque and opened fire around 2.45am," Ali said.Security forces exercised restraint during the operation to avoid damaging the mosque where Bhat had taken shelter. Ali said there was no urgency to conclude the operation at the cost of damaging the religious structure.Explaining why Bhat's killing was particularly significant, the SSP said the terrorist had joined LeT exactly a year earlier, on November 18, 2025, and had become heavily self-radicalised."This will be one of our biggest successes of 2026. He became active on this very day last year (November 18, 2025), joined Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), and was heavily self-radicalised. He was receiving instructions from across the border to disrupt peace, tourism, and the economy after carrying out 3–4 ruthless attacks," Ali said.Reacting to the operation, CRPF Director General GP Singh congratulated the personnel involved. articles.title: In 2007, a businessman paid $12.25 million for a Malibu mansion; the 2018 Woolsey Fire destroyed it, and the vacant 5.35-acre coastal plot is now headed to auction with a $12.99 million reserve
articles.summary: A Malibu property that once carried a $29.8 million asking price is heading to auction as a vacant, fire damaged coastal plot.
articles.body: A Malibu property that once carried a $29.8 million asking price is heading to auction as a vacant, fire damaged coastal plot. According to Realtor.com, Hong Kong multimillionaire Hiroshi Horiike paid $12.25 million for the Malibu Park mansion in 2007, but the home was destroyed in the 2018 Woolsey Fire and the 5.35 acre site is now being offered with a $12.99 million reserve bid.The property at 30601 Morning View Drive overlooks the Pacific Ocean, Zuma Beach, Broad Beach, and Catalina Island. Its story has moved from a high end purchase and a contentious real estate lawsuit to a devastating wildfire, and now to a sealed bid auction that could determine what rises on the land next.A mansion with a complicated pastHoriike bought the Malibu beach mansion in 2007 for $12.25 million. At the time, the property was marketed as a 15,000 square foot home, though later court proceedings found that the actual size was less than 10,000 square feet.In 2012, Horiike sued Coldwell Banker and broker Chris Cortazzo, alleging that the mansion’s size had been misrepresented during a previous sale attempt. He sought $5 million in damages, and the dispute eventually reached the California Supreme Court.The brokerage won the initial jury trial, but an appeals court ruled that dual agents owe fiduciary duties to both buyer and seller. At a retrial in April 2018, a second jury again sided with Coldwell Banker and Cortazzo.The fire changed everythingIn 2018, the Woolsey Fire destroyed the Malibu mansion. According to Realtor.com, the only thing reported to have survived was a marble statue of Horiike’s father.The loss left Horiike with a vacant 5.35 acre plot in one of Malibu’s most desirable coastal locations. The property had once been a private residence with sweeping ocean views, but its value now rests largely on the land, its location, and the possibility of rebuilding.The fire also reshaped the seller’s plans. Last year, the asking price had dropped to $19.9 million following the Palisades Fire, as buyer interest softened amid local fire damage and broader market pressures.Why the land still has valueDespite the destruction, the plot remains a rare piece of coastal real estate. It sits in Malibu Park and offers views of the ocean, Zuma Beach, Broad Beach, and Catalina Island, making it attractive to buyers seeking privacy, space, and a premium location.The auction includes approved plans by architect Clive Dawson for a seven bedroom, 10 bathroom home. The plans also call for a pool, tennis facilities, equestrian features, and a private pedestrian tunnel to Zuma Beach.Thanks to grandfathered Woolsey Fire rebuild protections, a buyer could construct a mansion of up to 14,500 square feet on the site. Realtor.com notes that this scale would be virtually impossible to replicate under current city limits, adding to the property’s appeal for developers and luxury homebuilders.How the auction worksThe sealed bid auction is being conducted by Paramount Realty USA in collaboration with listing broker Shamon Shamonki of Sotheby’s International Realty. Bids are due by December 3, according to Realtor.com.The reserve bid is set at $12.99 million, slightly above the $12.25 million Horiike paid for the original mansion in 2007. That figure gives potential buyers a clear starting point while leaving room for the final price to rise depending on interest.The auction approach reflects a shift in strategy. Rather than waiting for a buyer at a fixed asking price, the seller is testing the market directly and hoping that a competitive bidding process will produce a timely sale.What buyers are bidding onBuyers are not bidding on a finished home. They are bidding on a large, scenic Malibu parcel with existing approvals, rebuild protections, and a set of plans for a substantial new residence.The approved Clive Dawson plans offer a starting point for a luxury project, but the buyer would still need to complete construction. The property’s appeal lies in the combination of land, views, and the opportunity to build at a scale that current regulations may not allow elsewhere.For some buyers, the site could become a private estate. For others, it may represent an investment opportunity in one of California’s most exclusive coastal markets.A story of loss and opportunityThe property’s journey reflects how quickly circumstances can change in high end real estate. A mansion purchased for $12.25 million in 2007 became the centre of a legal dispute, was destroyed by wildfire, and is now being sold as vacant land with a reserve just above the original purchase price.For Horiike, the auction represents an effort to move on from a property that has been marked by loss. Shamonki, who also lost his family home in the 2025 Palisades fire, said the seller wanted to liquidate the property by the end of the year.For the buyer, the plot offers a chance to create something new on a rare piece of Malibu coastline. Whether the final bid reaches the reserve or goes higher, the auction will determine the next chapter for a property that has already seen more than its share of drama.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: BJP calls Rahul Gandhi 'Mir Jafar of India' over his remarks on economy in US
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's remarks on India's economy, unemployment and education system during an event at Columbia University in New York
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's remarks on India's economy, unemployment and education system during an event at Columbia University in New York drew sharp backlash from BJP leaders on Wednesday, who accused him of spreading “anti-India propaganda” while speaking abroad.Gandhi on Tuesday said India was heading towards an economic crisis, citing widespread unemployment and problems in the education system.During a press conference, BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia accused Rahul of being immature and anti-India."Today, every Indian feels ashamed by the baseless, false, and anti-India statements made by Rahul Gandhi on foreign soil to defame the country,” Bhatia said.“Rahul Gandhi is immature, anti-India, and the 'Mir Jafar' of India,” he added.Bhatia also alleged that Rahul travels abroad ahead of every Parliament session “to take guidance from his foreign masters?"Earlier, BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari also targeted Gandhi in a post on X, calling him the “leader of anti-India propaganda”.Bhandari accused him of insulting India at the university by describing its economy as being in a state of disaster and raising concerns about Indian democracy.BJP national spokesperson CR Kesavan said Gandhi followed a pattern of tarnishing India's image whenever he travelled abroad."Whenever Rahul Gandhi travels abroad, he follows a pernicious pattern of tarnishing India's image with his toxic lies,” Kesavan said, as per ANI news agency.Kesavan also contrasted Rahul's comments with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's conduct at the Quad Summit, alleging that while Modi respectfully picked up the Indian tricolour from the floor, Gandhi had cheered foreign delegates who mocked India.BJP Telangana president N Ramchander Rao also criticised Rahul, saying he had previously invited foreigners to speak against India on Indian soil and was now making critical remarks about the country during an overseas visit.“Yet again, Rahul Gandhi speaks against India and its economy on foreign soil. Until yesterday, he was inviting foreigners to speak against India on Indian soil. Now he has gone abroad and is speaking against the country,” Rao said.Referring to Gandhi's comments on the economy, unemployment and education, Rao questioned why foreign students were coming to Indian universities if the country's education system had collapsed. He also cited India's GDP growth and rising quarterly GST collections, claiming that the unemployment rate had fallen from 6 per cent to 3 per cent. Rao further referred to the World Economic Forum while claiming that the number of people living below the poverty line in India had declined.Bihar BJP president Sanjay Saraogi also accused the opposition leader of opposing India in the course of his political opposition to the BJP. He cited India's economic and military standing and Modi's global popularity, arguing that Gandhi's remarks about an impending economic crisis were disconnected from the country's position.“This is Rahul Gandhi's problem, while opposing the BJP, he has started opposing India,” Saraogi said, according to ANI.“That is why Congress has been wiped out in this country," he said, blaming the Congress leader's similar remarks for the party's electoral setbacks.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Long layover at Kochi railway stations? Southern Railway plans AC sleeping pods starting at Rs 99 an hour, with privacy doors, charging ports and Wi-Fi at Aluva and Ernakulam Junction
articles.summary: KOCHI: Southern Railway is planning to introduce air-conditioned executive lounges with sleeping pods at Aluva and Ernakulam Junction railway stations,
articles.body: KOCHI: Southern Railway is planning to introduce air-conditioned executive lounges with sleeping pods at Aluva and Ernakulam Junction railway stations, offering passengers a place to rest during long layovers, with hourly rates starting at Rs 99.The proposed facilities will be the first of their kind in the Thiruvananthapuram railway division. A senior railway official said tenders had been floated for the Aluva facility, which will come up on railway land opposite the KSRTC bus stand. Southern Railway will provide the land, while the selected bidder will construct and operate the lounge on a 10-year lease.At Aluva, the facility will occupy a two-storey building spread across 10,000 sq ft. At Ernakulam Junction, it will be built above the existing air-conditioned waiting room at the northern end of the main platform.The sleeping pods will be available on an hourly rental basis, unlike hotels that generally charge for a 24-hour stay. Starting at Rs 99 for an hour, each pod will have a reclining bed, individual climate control, a privacy door or lock, USB charging ports, a reading light and high-speed Wi-Fi.The facilities are aimed at passengers facing long gaps between connecting trains, delays or journeys at odd hours, providing them with a secure and comfortable place to rest.Meanwhile, Ernakulam Junction already has a 160-sq-ft air-conditioned waiting hall on platform one, which passengers can use for Rs 30 an hour. It is open to all valid ticket holders, including those travelling in general second class and platform ticket holders.The hall has 100 cushioned push-back seats with individual mobile charging points, free high-speed Wi-Fi, newspapers, a mini-library and a large television. It also has restrooms equipped with air purifiers, toilet facilities and a private feeding room for mothers.Similar air-conditioned sleeping-pod facilities are already operational at Kochi Metro's MG Road, Pathadipalam and Aluva stations. articles.title: In just one week, how security forces avenged attack on CRPF personnel in Kulgam
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Security forces on Wednesday eliminated top Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat in an encounter in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Security forces on Wednesday eliminated top Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat in an encounter in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district, avenging the attack on CRPF personnel. The terror strike, which left three security personnel injured, took place seven days ago.Bhat, described by security forces as the last active local terrorist in the Valley, was trapped inside a mosque after an extensive search operation involving CCTV footage and repeated intelligence inputs. He refused to surrender despite repeated appeals by security forces and was eventually neutralised.Union home minister Amit Shah hailed the operation, praising the "coordinated efforts" of the forces.Shah wrote on X, "With the coordinated efforts of JKP, Indian Army, CRPF and intelligence agencies, Lashkar's last known active local terrorist in the valley, Lateef Bhat, was neutralised in an operation in Kulgam in the early morning hours today. One of his terrorist associates, Umar Nisar, was also neutralised in Kulgam, the day before. The entire operation was marked by a very high level of synergy."Bhat's alleged associate, Umar Nisar Dar, had been killed two days earlier.Also Read| Trapped in Kulgam mosque, LeT commander Lateef Bhat refuses to surrenderNovember 11: Attack on CRPF post leaves three personnel injuredTwo armed men opened fire on a CRPF post in Akhran village in Kulgam district, injuring three personnel, one of them critically. Officials initially received reports that the attackers had arrived on a motorcycle. However, subsequent ground verification established that the two men had approached the checkpost on foot from a nearby forested area.According to officials, one attacker opened fire while the other provided cover. Both fled towards Naupur through the tree line. "The area has dense vegetation resembling a small forest, which the terrorists used as cover before and after the attack," an official told news agency PTI.Security forces launched a cordon-and-search operation, increased deployments and began examining CCTV footage from the surrounding areas.November 10-15: CCTV footage helps investigators trace movementsInvestigators examining footage from November 10 and 11 identified Bhat and Dar at multiple locations, including Mir Bazar, Akhran, Hablish and Kilam. According to police, the two had conducted reconnaissance at these locations to identify potential targets and plan attacks against security forces.The footage also documented their movements while fleeing after the November 11 attack on the CRPF naka at Akhran, police said.“During the analysis of CCTV footage from November 10 and 11, security agencies found both Umar Nisar Dar and Lateef Bhat captured on multiple CCTV cameras installed at the identified locations,” officials said.“The footage documented their movements while conducting reconnaissance and subsequently fleeing after the Akhran attack.”Investigators also found that Dar had allegedly been providing shelter and logistical assistance to Bhat for five to six months. His family had lodged a missing-person report at Kulgam police station after he disappeared. Investigators subsequently established that Dar had joined The Resistance Front (TRF), an offshoot of LeT, after the November 11 attack, officials said.Also Read| 'Some dishes best served cold': LeT commander Lateef Bhat killed in Kulgam encounterNovember 16: Umar Nisar Dar killed, Bhat escapesFollowing intelligence inputs about the movement of two suspected terrorists near Laru bypass, the Army and the Special Operations Group of Jammu and Kashmir Police launched a cordon-and-search operation.The suspects fled towards two nearby schools situated close to an apple orchard, where students were present. Officials said security forces prioritised evacuating the children before beginning the operation.The evacuation took around 90 minutes, according to officials quoted by PTI. Dar was subsequently killed in the encounter, while Bhat managed to escape.Officials said Bhat was believed to have sustained bullet injuries. Security forces continued searches across the surrounding area to trace him.November 17: Search operation widenedSecurity forces extended the search to dozens of villages around the encounter site, with drones and sniffer dogs deployed to locate Bhat. Officials said additional forces were positioned to strengthen the cordon, while teams searched suspected hideouts and carried out door-to-door searches at identified locations.The police also reiterated their findings about the alleged reconnaissance conducted by Bhat and Dar before the attack on the CRPF post. The prolonged security restrictions, however, drew criticism from political leaders in Kashmir, who said ordinary residents were facing hardship.November 18: Bhat trapped in Kulgam, refuses to surrenderActing on specific intelligence inputs, security forces launched another cordon-and-search operation in Zangalpora village in the Devsar area of south Kashmir.Officials said contact with Bhat was re-established early Wednesday morning, leading to a renewed encounter. The operation began before morning prayers, with security forces offering him an opportunity to surrender after trapping him inside the cordon.Videos of security personnel appealing to him to surrender circulated on social media. However, officials said Bhat refused.According to Kulgam Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Anayat Ali Chowdhary, the encounter escalated when the terrorist opened fire at around 2:45 pm."An encounter was initiated based on credible intelligence gathered through proper planning and a coordinated effort by the Jammu and Kashmir Police alongside other security forces, successfully cordoning off the area where a local terrorist named Lateef is trapped," Chowdhary said.He added, "Throughout this operation, security forces have maintained maximum restraint to protect the mosque situated within the cordon, strictly following standard operating procedures while handling the situation over time with patience and careful planning."The SSP said security forces attempted to persuade Bhat to surrender through a lengthy video call involving him, the SSP and the chief executive officer of the 9 Rashtriya Rifles."Despite these appeals, the terrorist refused to surrender and instead entered a mosque, prompting repeated public announcements urging him to come out," Chowdhary said. Police sources subsequently confirmed that Bhat had been killed. They said he was trapped inside the mosque during the operation and that no damage was caused to the structure.Reacting to the operation, Director General of the CRPF GP Singh posted on X, "Congratulations, guys. Some dishes are best served cold, even in cold weather."Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Apollo Hospitals opens specialised women and children's healthcare institute in Hyderabad
articles.summary: HYDERABAD: Apollo Hospitals on Tuesday inaugurated the Apollo Institute of Parents and Children at its Financial District facility, strengthening
articles.body: HYDERABAD: Apollo Hospitals on Tuesday inaugurated the Apollo Institute of Parents and Children at its Financial District facility, strengthening specialised healthcare services for women, mothers, newborns and children.The facility features a dedicated obstetrics wing, a Level III Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) and an attached perinatal centre to provide comprehensive care for mothers and newborns, including high-risk pregnancies and premature babies.The institute offers integrated services covering fertility counselling, fetal assessments, high-risk pregnancy management, maternity care, specialised labour and delivery services and general paediatric care.After inaugurating the facility, Upasana Kamineni Konidela, Director, Apollo Hospitals Projects, shared her personal experience of postpartum challenges following the birth of her twins and stressed the need for emotional and medical support for women during pregnancy and after childbirth."My postpartum journey with the twins was extremely tough. It is still too raw to talk about. Couples should not withdraw into a cocoon but come out and seek help and support," she added.Highlighting the importance of addressing women's health beyond childbirth, she said society celebrated pregnancy and delivery but often overlooked the emotional and physical challenges women faced during the fourth trimester. Comprehensive support should be available from the first trimester to the fourth, she added.Dr Phani Jyothsana, consultant gynaecologist, Apollo Financial District, said the institute aimed to provide personalised, multidisciplinary healthcare for women at every stage of life, along with specialised services for newborns and children. Its integrated approach would facilitate early diagnosis, timely intervention and coordinated treatment.Dr Pujitha Devi, consultant gynaecologist, said the institute was equipped with advanced intensive care facilities and specialised newborn care services. The NICU also incorporates Kangaroo Mother Care to support the health and development of newborns.The facility has also been designed to ensure patient comfort and convenience. It includes dedicated access for women and children, private consultation and procedure rooms, feeding lounges, comfortable inpatient facilities and child-friendly play areas.Mr Harkaran Singh Sahni, Chief Operating Officer, Apollo Hospitals, Financial District, said the new institute would further strengthen the hospital group's specialised women and children's healthcare services in Hyderabad and neighbouring regions.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. articles.title: Small island nations demand urgent climate action at UN talks as stakes rise
articles.summary: Small island nations are stepping up pressure on major economies at the United Nations climate negotiations, urging the international community to take
articles.body: Small island nations are stepping up pressure on major economies at the United Nations climate negotiations, urging the international community to take urgent action against global warming, which threatens their very survival.The annual climate conference has entered its second and final week in Turkey's resort city of Antalya. This year's discussions come after months of climate-related disasters, geopolitical disruptions and an intensifying El Nino phenomenon, all of which have increased the vulnerability of some of the world's smallest nations.“We don't need more studies. We don't need more negotiations. We just need more action,” Tonga prime minister Fatafehi Fakafanua told the associated press.Tonga, one of the world's major ocean nations, has a vast maritime territory compared with its relatively small land area. Like several other island countries, it faces serious threats from climate change. Record ocean temperatures endanger marine ecosystems that support local livelihoods, while melting glaciers contribute to rising sea levels, increasing the risks of coastal erosion and flooding.Tonga and other small island developing States (SIDS) have emerged as vocal advocates for climate action, urging larger and more industrialised countries to reduce greenhouse gas emissions before the consequences become irreversible.These island nations are also calling on wealthier countries, which contribute significantly to global pollution, to provide financial assistance for climate adaptation, damage mitigation and recovery from climate-related disasters.Individually, small island economies have limited influence in international negotiations. However, their collective voice carries greater weight, said Ilana Seid, chair of the Alliance of Small Island States and Palau's ambassador to the United Nations.“On our own, individual SIDS are small economies. We have little leverage, but when you put us together and we speak with one voice, we can speak pretty loudly and pretty strongly,” Seid said.Many commitments emerging from the annual climate negotiations remain voluntary and legally nonbinding. Countries have also failed to reach a comprehensive agreement on moving away from fossil fuels, the primary source of greenhouse gas emissions. These shortcomings have fuelled criticism of the conference of the parties (COP) process.Against this backdrop, political leaders, negotiators and environmental activists say COP31 must restore confidence in international climate negotiations and demonstrate that these meetings can translate commitments into meaningful action.“I feel that my future and the future of generations after me are on the line,” said Atiterentaai Rinimarawa, a 24-year-old youth representative from Kiribati.“We are not asking for sympathy, but we are calling for climate justice, stronger commitment and real action,” she added.Island nations seek greater influence in climate talksTurkey and Australia are jointly hosting COP31 this year. Pacific island representatives said their participation and influence have increased, particularly through Australia's involvement and Fiji's hosting of a preparatory climate meeting in October.“I absolutely think that our voice has been elevated,” Fakafanua said, adding that it reflected years of efforts by island nations to secure greater recognition in international climate discussions.He said it had taken until COP31 for these countries to occupy a more prominent position in the negotiations.The Alliance of small island states comprises 39 countries, which Seid described as a powerful negotiating bloc. Despite their geographical differences, island nations across the Pacific, Caribbean and Africa face similar climate vulnerabilities.“Our vulnerabilities are so consistent, regardless of if you're from the Pacific, or the Caribbean, or the African region,” Seid said, adding that the international spotlight on these countries had become brighter this year.Global climate targets, however, remain significantly off track. The United Nations has warned that the world is unlikely to achieve its goal of limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial levels.Small island nations are urging governments to preserve this target, arguing that exceeding it could have devastating consequences for their populations.“For us, it's really not a temperature threshold, it's a survival threshold,” said Adelle Thomas, senior director at the Natural Resources Defense Council and a native of the Bahamas.She said the key question was whether political leaders would match their commitments with the realities already confronting vulnerable communities.Climate action needs to move fasterAlthough the world could exceed the 1.5-degree warming threshold, international climate negotiations have helped prevent temperatures from rising even further, Thomas said. This demonstrates that the COP process has delivered results, although its pace has failed to match the speed of climate change.Thomas, who also serves as vice-chair of a working group of the Intergovernmental panel on climate change, said countries should not abandon the negotiations despite their limitations.“It is a long-term game, which unfortunately doesn't align with the level of impacts that we're seeing, but I don't think that we should give up on COP,” she said.The absence of the United States, the world's largest economy and one of its major greenhouse gas emitters, has added another challenge to this year's discussions. Washington has stayed away from the negotiations for the second consecutive year.Fakafanua acknowledged that the process could be frustrating but maintained that international climate cooperation remained necessary.“We've definitely made progress and we're better with COP than without,” he said.The Alliance of Small Island States is also seeking concrete financial commitments at COP31. It wants to secure $500 million for climate resilience programmes and another $200 million to strengthen early-warning systems for natural disasters.Fakafanua argued that countries suffering the consequences of climate change should receive financial support from those primarily responsible for causing it.“It's only fair that those who are suffering from the effects of climate change are assisted by those who were at fault,” he said.This year has brought additional challenges for island nations. Global ocean temperatures reached record highs in August, while an exceptionally strong El Nino continues to intensify. Geopolitical developments, including the war involving Iran, have also pushed up energy prices, adding to economic pressures.Thomas said climate change was no longer a distant international concern, as communities across the world were already experiencing its effects.“Average citizens around the world are experiencing climate impacts in their homes and in their communities and that directly links to what's going on in these international negotiations,” she said.She stressed that citizens and local communities also had a responsibility to hold their governments accountable and ensure that leaders prioritised climate action.COP31 is taking place amid competition for international attention, with other major global summits beginning in China and the Philippines.Qiyun Woo, a young environmental activist from Singapore, said the climate negotiations needed to rebuild confidence among younger generations and demonstrate that world leaders were committed to securing a sustainable future.“These climate talks need to renew faith,” Woo said, adding that young people needed to believe in international processes and the ability of global leaders to protect future generations.You use AI every day. articles.title: SCBA urges Supreme Court to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against advocate
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Bar Association on Tuesday moved a petition, with the attorney general R Venkataramani’s consent, requesting the SC to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Bar Association on Tuesday moved a petition, with the attorney general R Venkataramani’s consent, requesting the SC to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against advocate Pravin Singhal who on Monday had created an unruly scene inside the courtroom and questioned the CJI’s integrity.SCBA general secretary Pragya Baghel requested a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana for urgent listing of the petition. The CJI asked, “Why do you want to make a hero of that advocate?”But Baghel said that if such unruly and contemptuous behaviour is not nipped in the bud, it would cause grave damage to the image, dignity and reputation of the institution. The CJI agreed to list the matter as soon as possible.SCBA was activated into drafting a criminal contempt petition and sought the legally required consent of the AG after it received a written complaint from advocate Meenesh Dubey who witnessed the unsavoury behaviour of Singhal, who threw papers towards the CJI-led bench after questioning the integrity of the CJI for not listing a petition for hearing.SCBA said Singhal, after being removed from the courtroom by security personnel, continued shouting and using abusive and derogatory language against the CJI outside the courtroom. The AG gave consent for filing of the criminal contempt petition on Tuesday.“The dignity and authority of the SC is integral to maintenance of public confidence in the administration of justice and the Rule of Law. The deliberate and intentional scandalous statements (by the advocate) knowing that it would lower the authority of the SC warrants strict action against the Respondents in accordance with law,” it said.The association also referred to a Instagram post by Singhal in October in which he had used derogatory and scandalous remarks against the CJI, “repeatedly referring to the CJI as a ‘thief’, ‘fake and ‘an agent of the PM’, besides making other abusive remarks questioning his integrity and independence”.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: After losing her daughter to fentanyl poisoning, South Dakota journalist Angela Kennecke founded a nonprofit that has distributed over 15,700 naloxone kits, funded more than $500,000 in addiction treatment and reached 20,000 students
articles.summary: The death of her 21-year-old daughter Emily from fentanyl poisoning in 2018 changed the life of South Dakota journalist Angela Kennecke.
articles.body: The death of her 21-year-old daughter Emily from fentanyl poisoning in 2018 changed the life of South Dakota journalist Angela Kennecke. What began as a personal tragedy eventually became a mission to prevent other families from experiencing the same loss. Kennecke founded Emily's Hope, a nonprofit dedicated to tackling substance use disorders through overdose prevention, treatment assistance, education and recovery support. Since its inception, the organisation has distributed more than 15,700 naloxone kits, invested over $500,000 in treatment scholarships and taken substance-use prevention education into schools, reaching more than 20,000 students. From making overdose-reversal medication accessible to helping people afford rehabilitation, the initiative has grown into a multi-pronged effort to address the opioid crisis and challenge the stigma surrounding addiction.A daughter's fentanyl death inspired a journalist to help thousandsEmily Groth was 21 when she died from fentanyl poisoning in May 2018. According to her mother's account, Emily had believed she was obtaining heroin, but an autopsy revealed that fentanyl had caused her death.Kennecke, who had spent decades working as a television journalist, had been reporting on the opioid crisis when she received the news of her daughter's death. Emily was also just days away from entering a treatment programme.The loss prompted Kennecke to establish Emily's Hope in 2019, turning her daughter's memory into an initiative focused on preventing overdose deaths and improving access to addiction treatment.After 33 years in television journalism, Kennecke eventually left her newsroom career in 2022 to concentrate on running the nonprofit.Nonprofit distributes more than 15,700 naloxone kits to prevent overdosesOne of Emily's Hope's central initiatives is expanding access to naloxone, a medication that can rapidly reverse an opioid overdose. Also known by the brand name Narcan, it can restore normal breathing in someone experiencing an opioid overdose and provide time for emergency medical assistance to arrive.According to the organisation's 2025 annual report, Emily's Hope had distributed 15,732 naloxone kits cumulatively. More than 14,000 of those kits were distributed during 2025 alone.The nonprofit has also worked to make the medication accessible through public distribution boxes. Its network included 34 distribution boxes, while naloxone was stocked alongside automated external defibrillators and first-aid supplies at 340 locations.Its distribution efforts extended across 32 counties and six of South Dakota's nine tribal areas. The organisation also expanded its work into Iowa.In April 2025, Emily's Hope became part of a wider state initiative involving South Dakota's Attorney General's Office and state health and social services departments. The partnership aimed to distribute 20,000 naloxone kits, containing 40,000 doses, using funding from opioid settlements and support from pharmaceutical company Teva.More than $500,000 towards addiction treatmentBeyond overdose prevention, Emily's Hope works to address another major barrier faced by people struggling with substance use disorders: the cost of treatment.The organisation provides treatment scholarships to individuals who need financial assistance to access rehabilitation and recovery services. Its 2025 annual report recorded a cumulative investment of $505,494.92 in treatment scholarships, supporting 297 individuals.During 2025, the nonprofit provided $79,080.74 in scholarships to 52 people.One of the stories highlighted in the report is that of Lori Kellar, who struggled with alcohol use disorder and experienced difficulties in her personal relationships. Financial assistance from Emily's Hope helped her access 28 days of intensive treatment at the Avera Addiction Care Center.Following treatment, Kellar entered recovery, completed pharmacy technician training and worked towards rebuilding her relationship with her husband.Taking addiction prevention education into schoolsEmily's Hope has also expanded its efforts beyond people already affected by substance use disorders, focusing on educating children about prevention and healthy decision-making.Its school curriculum introduces students to topics such as how substances affect the brain and body, medication safety, emotional regulation, peer pressure and the importance of making healthy choices.The programme uses a strategy called Pause-Think-Act to encourage children to consider the consequences of their decisions before responding to challenging situations.According to the organisation's 2025 annual report, its curriculum reached more than 18,000 students during that year across 44 school districts.
